audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, rule 01: unstressed presyllable + stressed main syllable) rests on the standard 392-pp reference grammar (So-Hartmann 2009), which I downloaded from the STEDT site and in which the deciding quotation appears verbatim at sec. 2.1, printed p. 35; the whole stress treatment (pp. 35-37) is unhedged and matches the classification, and every stress mention in the book is in that section. Two further open sources downloaded now agree: Hartmann 2001 (LTBA 24.2, p.124) states the syllabic-nasal and glottal presyllables are unstressed; Mortensen 2023 (Himalayan Linguistics) restates the Daai sesquisyllabic minor+major structure without a stress claim; Hartmann-So 1989 is silent on stress. No copies we hold existed before this reading; the source is now Housekeeping only: repair the truncated cite string ('via extracted text

sources.citation: So-Hartmann 2009, A Descriptive Grammar of Daai Chin, STEDT Monograph 7, sec. 2.1 (PDF re-read via(2026-08-31)
sources.quote: That is, the PW is always constituted of a stressed syllable 'S, which may optionally be preceded by an unstressed syllabic constituent (S). I will refer to the preposed unstressed element as a PRESYLLABLE and the stressed one as the MAIN SYLLABLE.

sources.citation: So-Hartmann, Helga. 2009. A Descriptive Grammar of Daai Chin. STEDT Monograph Series 7. Berkeley: Sino-Tibetan Etymological Dictionary and Thesaurus Project, University of California. 392 pp. (open PDF from stedt.johnblowe.com/pubs_and_prods/)

sources.quote: 'the PW is always constituted of a stressed syllable 'S, which may optionally be preceded by an unstressed syllabic constituent (S)' (p.35); 'These two-syllabic phonological words involve a weakly stressed syllable (WS) closely-knit with a following strongly stressed dominant or main syllable (SS)... metrically iambic contours' (p.35); 'no other phonological material may be inserted between the Presyllable and the Mainsyllable, that is, the sequence constitutes a cohesive stress contour' (p.36); presyllable inventory reduced to syllabic m-, n-, ng-, glottal, and vowel a- (p.37).

sources.quote: 'The syllabic nasals and syllabic [ʔ] are unstressed syllables, and the transition between these elements and the following initial consonant of a noun or verb root is a very close one.'

sources.quote: Describes Daai (after So-Hartmann 2009: 38) as sesquisyllabic with minor syllables that 'often consist of a single consonant without a vocalic nucleus' preceding full major syllables; no explicit statement of stress placement.
